items.headline: Daniels (elbow) completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Giants. He also threw a successful two-point conversion.
items.summary: Daniels wasn't afraid to run in his return from a two-game absence due to a dislocated left elbow. He scored second-half rushing touchdowns of 38 and 26 yards, the latter of which Daniels followed up with a two-point conversion to Terry McLaurin to give the Commanders a 14-point lead with 11:05 left in the fourth quarter. The Giants proceeded to erase that deficit and force OT, where Daniels drove the Commanders down to the Giants' 24-yard line with 55 seconds remaining, but Washington remarkably failed to get a game-winning field-goal attempt off, as the Commanders ran the clock down and then failed to stop the clock when Daniels went down inbounds on their final offensive play. The bizarre ending overshadows what was otherwise an encouraging performance from Daniels, who made it through the game without any physical setbacks and is set to start in Week 6 against the 49ers.

items.headline: Allen completed 12 of 19 passes for 210 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding 10 carries for 121 yards and another score and a two-point conversion pass in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win against the Rams on Monday night.
items.summary: Facing a Rams defense that had forced plenty of inefficiency through the air from both wide receivers and tight ends and operating without both DJ Moore (shoulder) and Joshua Palmer (shoulder), Allen unsurprisingly recorded a season low in completions. However, the prolific signal-caller more than made up for it on the ground with a season-high rushing yardage total, as well as his eighth rushing touchdown of the season. Allen's most crucial runs outside of his one-yard scoring dive early in the fourth quarter came on Buffalo's final drive in overtime, when he rattled off 19- and 13-yard scrambles to move the ball from the Bills' 41-yard line to the Rams' 27-yard line to set up an eventual game-winning field goal from Tyler Bass. Allen also added his seventh passing score of the season late in the third quarter on a seven-yard strike to Keon Coleman, and the two-time All-Pro will next turn his sights to a Week 6 road matchup against the Raiders on Sunday.

Darnold's second pick did ultimately help lead to the loss, as it came on the first drive of overtime at the Seahawks' 43-yard line to set the Broncos up on the edge of field-goal range. Darnold's yardage total was his second highest of the season, but he's been much more mistake-prone early in the 2026 campaign while throwing seven interceptions, half of his 2025 total. items.headline: Prescott completed 24 of 42 passes for 316 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers on Thursday night.
items.summary: Prescott's final yardage number was sure to please fantasy managers, but there was a pretty sizable gulf between that figure and the veteran signal-caller's actual play-to-play performance most of the night. Prescott and the air attack struggled through more than a half against an aggressive Buccaneers defense, including on a third-quarter interception that led to a Tampa Bay touchdown. However, he came alive on a mid-fourth-quarter drive where the Cowboys sped up the pace, capping that 10-play, 99-yard possession off with an 18-yard touchdown pass to George Pickens. Prescott had Dallas moving again the next time he had the ball, but a pass that went off Jake Ferguson's hands over the middle was secured by Alex Anzalone for what turned out to be a game-sealing interception. Prescott completed a season-low 57.1 percent of his throws and failed to throw multiple touchdown passes for the third straight game, but he'll still take an impressive 9:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 road showdown against the Packers on Sunday night, Oct. 18.

The second-year player out of USC ended up taking the field for 56 of 66 snaps, finishing with 62 yards on 15 carries to go with four catches for 23 yards on four targets. With Montgomery on track to miss at least the London game and potentially additional contests beyond that, Marks should have a decent chance at replicating his Week 5 touch count. items.summary: Stafford's stellar final line underscores he did everything within his power to lead the Rams to victory, as the reigning MVP finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season and fourth 300-yard effort of the campaign. The night also marked Stafford's third multi-TD tally over the first five games, with his scoring strikes going to Davante Adams (four and five yards) and Puka Nacua (two yards). Nacua also was on the receiving end of a whopping 17 of Stafford's completions and the intended target on 24 of his pass attempts, but all of those efforts went for naught thanks to the Bills' block of a Harrison Mevis 48-yard field-goal attempt in overtime that would have sealed the victory for Los Angeles. After posting just 96 scoreless yards through three games, Nabers has built momentum heading into a Week 6 home game against the Saints, with 233 receiving yards and two touchdown catches across his last two outings.

items.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that Wilson (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
items.summary: Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reported earlier Monday that Wilson is expected to miss at least a couple of weeks due to a finger injury that he sustained during the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday, so the third-year receiver's absence could extend into Week 7. While the Steelers are without Wilson, Ben Skowronek (leg) and Michael Pittman (foot) for at least Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, quarterback Aaron Rodgers is left with wideouts  DK Metcalf, rookie Germie Bernard, running back Jaylen Warren and tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth as his main targets in the passing game.

items.headline: What to know before setting your lineup for Week 5: Is Maye back? Start Wilson?
items.summary: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 5.

items.headline: The Steelers placed Pittman (foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: With the expected move now official, Pittman will be required to miss at least the next four games, making Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15 the earliest that the veteran wide receiver can return. Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard are both in line for more offensive snaps for as long as Pittman is sidelined.

items.headline: Steelers place WR Michael Pittman Jr. on IR with foot injury
items.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers placed wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve, the team announced on Saturday.

items.headline: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman aggravates foot, out weeks
items.summary: Steelers receiver Michael Pittman Jr. aggravated a foot injury and is out multiple weeks.

items.headline: Evans (ribs/Achilles) was a non-participant at Friday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
items.summary: Evans was spotted working on the side at the start of Friday's session, but with no activity for a second day in a row, he now has just one more chance to mix into drills Saturday before the 49ers potentially tag him with a designation ahead of Monday's game against the Commanders. There's more cause for concern this week due to the 49ers adding 'Achilles' next to his name on the injury report, and head coach Kyle Shanahan has termed the new issue "soreness," according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

items.headline: Mike Evans stars in 49ers' win: 'Exactly why he's here'
items.summary: Mike Evans had seven catches, 113 yards and a touchdown to push the unbeaten Niners (5-0, 3-0 NFC West) to a rousing 32-29 victory over the Seahawks.

items.headline: McCaffrey making the most of his touches
items.summary: Nick Wagoner discusses Christian McCaffrey's workload ahead of the 49ers' Week 6 matchup.

items.headline: McCaffrey rushed 11 times for 68 yards and a touchdown while catching all three of his targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks.
items.summary: McCaffrey gave the 49ers a 14-10 lead with an 11-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. His 14 touches tied a season low, and McCaffrey has yet to reach 20 touches in a game, as the undefeated 49ers have been content to manage his workload to some extent in order to keep the star running back fresh after McCaffrey averaged over 24 touches per game in the 2025 regular season. The reduced workload hasn't kept McCaffrey from scoring five touchdowns across his last four games, and he'll look to extend his four-game scoring streak in Week 6 against the Commanders.

items.headline: Christian McCaffrey, Olivia Culpo announce birth of second child
items.summary: McCaffrey and his wife, Olivia Culpo, announced the news of the birth of their second child in a joint post on Instagram on Saturday.

items.headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Thursday that the 49ers will "hold off" on placing Samuel (hamstring) on IR due to the team's bye in Week 8, Vic Tafur of the Athletic reports.
items.summary: It was reported earlier in the week that Samuel would miss multiple weeks; however, the 49ers are stopping short of placing him on injured reserve for the time being due to how the schedule sets up. Samuel is set to miss at least the Week 6 game against the Commanders and likely the following game against the Falcons before the team gets a bye. Week 9 seems to be the earliest potential return date for the veteran.

items.headline: Shanahan says 49ers WR Deebo Samuel to miss time with hamstring injury
items.summary: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel is expected to miss "at least a couple of weeks" with the hamstring injury he suffered Sunday in Seattle, coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday.

items.headline: 49ers lose WR Deebo Samuel to hamstring injury vs. Seahawks
items.summary: The 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel due to a hamstring injury in the third quarter, leaving San Francisco with just three healthy wideouts to finish Sunday's game vs. the Seahawks.

items.headline: Smith-Njigba brought in 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
items.summary: Despite the Broncos being down Pat Surtain (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks' air attack as a whole couldn't get much going through the first half-plus of play. The All-Pro receiver turned it on in the later portion of the contest, however, and he ultimately finished with season highs in receptions and targets, along with his second-highest amount of receiving yards. Smith-Njigba already has five 100-yard efforts in his first six games of the season, and his tendency to dominate Sam Darnold's attention once again will make him an elite option in all formats during a Week 7 Sunday night home showdown against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

items.headline: Knockout league pickups: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Ja'Marr Chase among big names available in Week 5
items.summary: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.

items.headline: Week 4 winners and losers: Tetairoa McMillan, CeeDee Lamb dominate; Jaxon Smith-Njigba struggles
items.summary: CeeDee Lamb and Kyren Williams came up big in Week 4, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D'Andre Swift had disappointing days.

items.headline: Daniels will be the Buccaneers' starting quarterback against the Steelers after Baker Mayfield (right thumb) was ruled out.
items.summary: It will be Daniels' third consecutive start under center, as Mayfield continues to be sidelined by a dislocated right thumb that prevented the veteran from practicing all week. Daniels led the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season in Week 5 against the Cowboys, when he completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown while turning seven carries into 23 yards.

items.headline: Undrafted rookie QB Daniels savors Thursday night win vs. Cowboys
items.summary: Jalon Daniels became the first undrafted rookie starting QB in the common draft era to win a game for a team that entered winless, leading the Bucs to a 24-16 win over the Cowboys.

items.headline: Buccaneers explode in third quarter against Cowboys to get first win
items.summary: Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and Tampa Bay held off Dallas on "Thursday Night Football."

items.headline: Mayfield (thumb) will not play Sunday, Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
items.summary: Head coach Todd Bowles confirmed what had been made obvious by Mayfield's continued absence from practices. There hasn't been anything said about his Week 7 chances, but the fact that it wasn't even a close call for Week 6 isn't the best sign. Jalon Daniels will make another start Sunday against Pittsburgh.

items.summary: Is Baker Mayfield really the worst QB in the NFC South?

items.headline: Sources: Baker Mayfield return hinges on when QB can grip football
items.summary: Baker Mayfield is expected to miss anywhere from three to six weeks, sources told ESPN, depending on how quickly the Buccaneers quarterback can grip the football.

items.headline: Pollard was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice due to rest.
items.summary: Pollard had been listed on Titans injury reports each of the last three weeks due to either a foot or ankle issue, but his absence from practice Wednesday was a result of planned maintenance rather than any sort of health concern. The 29-year-old will likely return to practice Thursday and should be ready to handle a lead role out of the backfield Sunday at Indianapolis.

items.headline: Mariota (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
items.summary: Mariota was forced to miss the Commanders' contest versus the Giants in Week 5 after spraining his MCL in Week 4 versus the Colts, and now his availability for Monday's game at San Francisco is in doubt. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday or Saturday, rookie seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis projects to continue to operate as Jayden Daniels' primary backup in Week 6.

items.headline: MCL sprain sidelines Mariota; Daniels preps for full practice
items.summary: In his team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL of his right knee, and the timetable for his return remains uncertain coach Dan Quinn said on Monday.

items.headline: Marcus Mariota out as Commanders turn to rookie Athan Kaliakmanis
items.summary: Marcus Mariota left Sunday's game against the Colts with a knee injury, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback.

items.headline: Wilson brought in four of seven targets for 30 yards and completed his only pass attempt for seven yards in the Cardinals' 45-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Wilson wasn't able to approach his usual elevated numbers against a Lions defense that had struggled against the pass. The typically busy receiver still finished tied for third in targets and also slotted in third in receptions, but Wilson ultimately generated his second-lowest reception and receiving yardage tallies of 2026. Marvin Harrison was traded to the Texans earlier Sunday, so despite Wilson's quiet afternoon, fantasy managers now know  Wilson will have one fewer competitor for targets from Jacoby Brissett moving forward.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Jackson to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Jackson was recently cut from the Ravens' practice squad. The 26-year-old has appeared in eight games combined for the Bengals and Raiders since 2023, totaling four catches for 56 yards and one touchdown.

items.headline: London caught seven of 11 targets for 118 yards in Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: London has recorded at least 96 receiving yards in three consecutive games since Michael Penix (ribs) made his season debut after missing the first two games of the season due to a knee injury, but Atlanta's top wideout is still searching for his first touchdown of the season. Penix sustained a rib injury late in the fourth quarter, and London had a 20-yard catch in overtime on a pass from Tua Tagovailoa, but Tagovailoa's next pass intended for London resulted in a game-losing interception. London should continue to lead Atlanta's passing game regardless of whom the Falcons start under center in Week 6 against the Bears.

items.headline: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Hurts, Jackson ruled out; Flowers to play
items.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.

items.headline: Flowers (toe) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game at Cleveland.
items.summary: The Ravens added Flowers to their injury report Thursday as a limited participant, and while he remained limited Friday, his game availability isn't in doubt. Tyler Huntley is making another start at quarterback with Lamar Jackson (ankle) ruled out again.

items.headline: Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards while catching one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons. He also ran in a two-point conversion.
items.summary: Henry unsurprisingly worked as the focal point of Baltimore's offense in the absence of Lamar Jackson (ankle). The star running back pulled the Ravens within two points with his 18-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Baltimore's two-point conversion attempt after that touchdown failed, but Henry took matters into his own hands to convert a game-tying two-point conversion out of the wildcat formation with 40 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He then tacked on 32 rushing yards on Baltimore's touchdown drive in OT to top the century mark on the ground for the first time since Week 1. Henry has opened his 11th NFL season with a five-game touchdown streak, producing seven rushing touchdowns and one receiving score ahead of a Week 6 trip to Cleveland.

items.headline: Fantasy football: Why now is the ideal time to trade Derrick Henry
items.summary: The ageless back is off to a strong start, which presents the opportunity to maximize the return in a deal.

items.headline: Coleman caught a seven-yard touchdown pass on two targets during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
items.summary: It was a statistically quiet night for Coleman despite the fact that DJ Moore (shoulder) was inactive, but Josh Allen completed only 12 of 19 passes and the Bills got most of their yardage on the ground. Coleman did have catches of 17 and seven yards in the third quarter negated by penalties, but the third-year pro was wide open for his touchdown after two Rams defensive backs collided. Coleman's 45 offensive snaps led all Bills wide receivers, and he has a 15-224-2 receiving line on 18 targets through five regular-season games. The Bills will stay on the road for Week 7 against the Raiders on Sunday, and Coleman's role on offense would shrink if Moore is cleared to return.

items.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Kirk Cousins, Keon Coleman lead top options
items.summary: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.

items.headline: Palmer (shoulder) and DJ Moore (shoulder) are listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Both wideouts missed Monday's win over the Rams, in which each of Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir and Skyler Bell topped 60 percent route share, though many of those routes were on plays that ended up being Josh Allen scrambles. Bell likely will lose the most playing time if Moore and/or Palmer returns this week.

items.headline: Bills rule out Ed Oliver, Joshua Palmer, wait on WR DJ Moore
items.summary: Bills wide receiver DJ Moore returned to practice in a noncontact jersey and will be designated as questionable for "Monday Night Football" against the Rams. Buffalo has ruled out wide receiver Joshua Palmer and defensive tackle Ed Oliver.

items.headline: Taylor Moton among 3 Panthers activated ahead of Eagles game
items.summary: The Panthers will have RT Taylor Moton and DE Tershawn Wharton available Sunday against the Eagles. RB Trevor Etienne was also activated off IR.

items.headline: Etienne (ankle) is listed as questionablefor Sunday's game against the Eagles.
items.summary: Etienne was a full practice participant all week, while AJ Dillon (ankle) was absent and has already been ruled out for Sunday. Etienne might've taken over the No. 2 RB role even if Dillon had stayed healthy, so it remains to be seen how that play out if/when both are available at the same time. The Panthers will need to activate Etienne from injured reserve by Saturday evening to have him available for Sunday's game. If they don't do that, they'll need to look to the practice squad for depth behind Chuba Hubbard.

items.headline: Kyle Monangai, Chuba Hubbard starred in superb week for Africa's running backs in NFL
items.summary: The Chicago Bears' Kyle Monangai (ties to Cameroon) and the Carolina Panthers' Chuba Hubbard (ties to Nigeria) starred in an NFL week which saw running backs with links to Africa impress.

items.headline: Hubbard rushed 20 times for 122 yards and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for seven yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.summary: Hubbard complemented Tetairoa McMillan's pair of receiving touchdowns with rushing scores of 15 yards in the first quarter and four yards in the third quarter. After handling 27 touches in Carolina's first two games, Hubbard has been leaned on for 44 touches across the most recent two games as the Panthers play without Jonathon Brooks (abdomen), who was placed on injured reserve Sept. 23. Hubbard will rest up during the Week 5 bye before getting a chance to add to his season totals of 390 scrimmage yards and five total TDs in Week 6 against the Eagles.

items.headline: Waller (toe) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.
items.summary: Waller should be fine to handle his usual role after upgrading to full practice participation Friday. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday, coming out of a Week 5 bye.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups for Week 4: Raymond, Waller among top options
items.summary: If injuries or tough matchups have you seeking help, Matt Bowen provides options at each key position.

items.headline: Panthers put Legette on IR; Coker also likely out vs. Lions
items.summary: The Panthers have placed 2024 first-round pick Xavier Legette on injured reserve ahead of Sunday's primetime matchup against the Lions. Wide receiver Jalen Coker is also unlikely to play against the Lions, sources told ESPN.

items.headline: The Panthers placed Legette (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Legette has been working through a knee injury the last two weeks, and while he was slated to miss a second straight contest Sunday against the Lions, he'll now sit out at least the next four (including Week 4), meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 8 versus the Broncos. In Legette's continued absence, Carolina will lean on Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker (quadriceps), Brycen Tremayne, John Metchie and David Moore at wide receiver.

items.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Atlanta, but if he's not given the green light to return, then it's unclear whether Keenum or Tyson Bagent starts under center for Chicago, Larry Mayer of the Bears' official site reports.
items.summary: It seems Keenum and Bagent would each have a 50-50 shot at starting Sunday if Williams isn't cleared to play, with head coach Ben Johnson saying Friday "we have two guys that are equally qualified" in reference to Keenum and Bagent. Keenum was the backup for each of the Bears' last two games, though he did take over in the fourth quarter of Chicago's Week 5 loss to Green Bay after Bagent threw his second pick of the game in the third period. Keenum was the starter and led the Bears to a Week 3 victory over the Eagles, when he completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns while adding six yards and a score on four carries.

items.headline: Bears call Case Keenum co-start a 'ceremonial first pitch'
items.summary: Both Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum started Sunday's game for the Bears, with coach Ben Johnson calling it a "ceremonial first pitch" of sorts for the latter.

items.headline: Raymond caught three of four passes for six yards and logged one carry for minus-2 yards during the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also returned one punt for nine yards.
items.summary: Two of Raymond's four touches resulted in negative yards, and the veteran wide receiver has logged six receiving yards in each of his last two games after producing a 19-214-1 receiving line on 21 targets through Chicago's first three games. He's reverted to the WR3 role behind Luther Burden and Rome Odunze, but the entire offense would have its floor raised if Caleb Williams (hamstring) is cleared to return for Week 7 against the Falcons this Sunday.

items.headline: Week 5 winners and losers: Maye, Warren, Gibbs dominate; Taylor, Brown struggle
items.summary: Drake Maye, Jaylen Warren and Jahmyr Gibbs came up big in Week 5, while Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown had disappointing days.

items.headline: Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and brought in three of four targets for 21 yards in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: As his final numbers corroborate, Brown found efficiency on the ground elusive against a surprisingly game Dolphins defense. The versatile back made a serviceable impact as a complementary option in the passing game, although his lost fumble came after a three-yard reception just past the midway point of the second quarter. Brown also saw Samaje Perine get some significant second-half run and ultimately outpace him by one rush attempt, but the former should remain the lead option in the ground attack coming out of a Week 6 bye in a Week 7 road matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25.

items.headline: Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson out for season with torn pec
items.summary: Bengals TE Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral in last Sunday's win over the Dolphins that will sideline him for the season, his agent told ESPN.

items.headline: Hudson's agent revealed Tuesday that the tight end sustained a torn pectoral in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Dolphins and is expected to miss the rest of the season, Charlie Clifford of WLWT News 5 Cincinnati reports.
items.summary: Hudson will presumably need surgery to address the pec tear and is likely to be placed on injured reserve in the coming days. Though he didn't win a spot on the Bengals' initial 53-man roster coming out of the preseason, Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the team's firs three games before getting signed to the roster Sept. 29. Over his four appearances with Cincinnati, the reserve tight end tallied seven catches for 33 yards and a touchdown on seven targets.

items.headline: Samaje Perine gives Bengals a strong jolt to end 2-game skid
items.summary: When the run game was struggling, the Bengals turned to Perine, whose downhill style paid dividends.

items.headline: Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards while catching both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 31-24 win over Miami.
items.summary: Perine surprisingly logged one more carry than starting running back Chase Brown (13) in the contest. Additionally, although he saw two fewer targets than Brown, Perine was able to reach paydirt in the second quarter, reeling in a six-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. Perine remains a highly valuable insurance policy for fantasy managers with Brown on their roster. Through five games, the 31-year-old has rushed 27 times for 110 yards while reeling in seven of 10 targets for 61 yards and a score.

items.headline: Badie (thumb) won't return to Thursday's game against Seattle, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports. He finished with one carry for six yards.
items.summary: Badie suffered a thumb injury in the first half and was considered questionable to return. Now that he has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's contest, RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins should each get a few more touches.

items.headline: Do the Broncos have a reliable No. 1 running back? Sorting Denver's backfield
items.summary: The Broncos' running game has been stuck in neutral, as J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie have struggled in the early going.

items.headline: Sutton brought in two of three targets for 19 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
items.summary: Sutton tied for third in receptions and targets while holding the same slotting in receiving yards for the Broncos on a night when Bo Nix could manage only 107 passing yards. The veteran wideout also took a hard hit on the one target he couldn't corral, and Sam Jane of The Denver Post reported Sutton was seen bent over and slightly limping on the sideline but never required a trip to the medical tent. Like fellow wideout Jaylen Waddle, the long-time Bronco's production has suffered as a result of Nix's tendency to stick to a very short-area passing attack this season, as Sutton is averaging a career-low 9.5 yards per reception heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

items.headline: Yes, it's OK to drop these underperformers from your fantasy football team
items.summary: You don't have to hold on to Justin Herbert, Kenny Gainwell, Coutland Sutton or other fantasy underperformers.

items.headline: Waddle secured four of seven targets for 24 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
items.summary: Waddle exited the game briefly due to a shoulder injury, but he was still able to finish as the Broncos' reception and targets leader on the night. His yardage total, modest as it was, also qualified him for runner-up status in that category on a night when Bo Nix threw for only 107 yards and averaged 4.0 yards per attempt. Waddle's production has suffered collateral damage from Nix's constant short-area throwing thus far this season, as the veteran receiver is averaging a career-low 10.4 yards per reception and just 38.0 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

items.headline: Where is Jaylen Waddle? Broncos' big offseason acquisition is off to slow start
items.summary: With just 204 receiving yards through five games, Jaylen Waddle has been mostly contained and hasn't yet made the impact the Broncos hoped. What has gone wrong?

items.headline: Week 5 winners and losers: Maye, Warren, Gibbs dominate; Taylor, Brown struggle
items.summary: Drake Maye, Jaylen Warren and Jahmyr Gibbs came up big in Week 5, while Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown had disappointing days.

items.headline: St. Brown secured six of 11 targets for 69 yards and committed two fumbles that remained with Detroit in the Lions' 45-21 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: St. Brown fell below his usual lofty standards with his numbers, but the star receiver still finished with team-high reception and target totals while also slotting in as the runner-up in receiving yards. St. Brown remains as integral a component of the Lions' air attack as ever, as he now has back-to-back 11-target games and has already seen 57 passes come his way overall in the first five contests of the campaign. St. Brown has turned those opportunities into a 37-372-5 line, and he'll be looking to snap a two-game touchdown drought when the Lions return to action in a NFC North home clash against the Packers on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

items.headline: Packers' Watson-Golden WR combo reminiscent of Nelson-Cobb
items.summary: It has been more than a decade since Green Bay had a dominant WR duo, but Watson and Golden are making their mark.

items.headline: Golden secured six of seven targets for 123 yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday. He also returned two punts for 27 yards.
items.summary: As good as Golden's afternoon was, he was actually slightly outshined by fellow wideout Christian Watson, who had 20 more receiving yards on the same number of catches and one additional target. Nevertheless, Golden's afternoon included a new career high in receiving yards, as well as a career-high-tying reception total. The second-year speedster is already well on his way to a breakout campaign, and he now has had at least seven targets in four of his first five games. The 2025 first-round pick will take a 24-397-2 line on 44 targets into a favorable Week 6 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

items.headline: Why Mike Clay is not interested in MarShawn Lloyd in Week 6
items.summary: Why Mike Clay is not interested in MarShawn Lloyd in Week 6

items.headline: Lloyd rushed 10 times for 31 yards and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for six yards during Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears.
items.summary: Lloyd was able to open the second quarter with a 10-yard touchdown run before later adding a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. The running back's 10 carries were his most since logging 13 rushes for 37 yards in Week 1 versus Minnesota. Lloyd has now compiled 112 rushing yards on 40 carries and two touchdowns while reeling in 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score over five games to open the 2026 season while operating as Green Bay's primary option in the backfield with Josh Jacobs (personal) on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

items.headline: Why Dopp is locking Jordan Love in as a top-7 QB in Week 6
items.summary: Why Dopp is locking Jordan Love in as a top-7 QB in Week 6

items.headline: Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding one carry for six yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
items.summary: Love was in prime form all afternoon against the Packers' long-time arch-rival, finishing with the third-highest single-game passing yardage total of his career while facilitating 100-yard efforts for both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The veteran signal-caller connected with the former for both of his touchdown passes, which came from 42 and 53 yards out in the first and third quarters, respectively. Love already has a trio of 300-yard games on the season and a 10:3 TD:INT heading into a Week 6 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. latest in Texans' quest to solve their WR2 conundrum
items.summary: Houston has traded and drafted receivers, hoping to complement No. 1 wideout Nico Collins and QB C.J. Stroud.

items.headline: Collins caught five of seven targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 26-3 win over the Titans.
items.summary: The Texans got right on both sides of the ball in their first win of the season, with Collins leading the team in targets and tying Jaylin Noel for the lead in receptions while Xavier Hutchinson topped them both in receiving yards. The trio will get some additional competition as soon as a Week 6 clash with Jacksonville after Houston traded for Marvin Harrison on Sunday, but Collins should remain the top option for C.J. Stroud as long as he remains healthy. Through three games this season, Collins has a 19-249-3 line on 25 targets.

items.headline: Dopp's hesitancy over starting Josh Downs in Week 6
items.summary: Dopp's hesitancy over starting Josh Downs in Week 6

items.headline: Downs (rest/hamstring) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.
items.summary: Downs was listed as limited Wednesday due to rest and a hamstring injury. The inclusion of rest in the reason for his limitations suggested the wide receiver wasn't dealing with a significant injury, but it's still encouraging to see that notion confirmed one day later with Downs' return to full participation. Downs is set to maintain a prominent role in Indianapolis' passing game Sunday against the 0-5 Titans.

items.headline: Jones completed 24 of 44 passes for 267 yards without a touchdown or interception and added four rushing yards on three carries in Sunday's 34-22 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: The Colts' lone TD came on a one-yard plunge by tight end Tyler Warren in the second quarter, and the rest of their points came via five Spencer Shrader field goals as Jones couldn't get the ball into the end zone. Jones still has yet to re-discover the form he displayed prior to the Achilles injury that ended his 2025 campaign, and through five games this season he's managed a weak 3:4 TD:INT and 5.8 YPA, although a depleted WR room is playing a large part in his downturn as well. Jones will try to build some momentum in Week 6 against the winless Titans.

items.headline: Despite Daniel Jones' struggles, Colts win second straight
items.summary: Jones has lost three fumbles over the past two weeks, but the Colts won both games.

items.headline: Hunter recorded a nine-yard reception and tallied six tackles and a pass breakup in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles in London.
items.summary: After not getting any run on offense in the Jaguars' Week 4 win over the Bengals, Hunter ended up taking the field for six of 72 snaps in Week 5 and was able to come away with his second reception of the season. The two-way player continues to see the overwhelming amount of his playing time on defense, where he was on the field for all 62 snaps. Expect the Jaguars continue to use Hunter almost exclusively at cornerback while sprinkling him into the offensive game plan only occasionally.

items.headline: Travis Hunter jukes Tee Higgins in Jags win, goes viral despite penalty
items.summary: Jacksonville's two-way star showed off his open-field agility before a penalty negated the play.

items.headline: Is Brenton Strange a good fantasy play vs. Texans?
items.summary: Is Brenton Strange a good fantasy play vs. Texans?

items.headline: Strange caught seven of eight targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: After breaking out for a 7-95-0 line last week, Strange tied that season high in catches, although for less yardage. The tight end is re-establishing himself as Trevor Lawrence's preferred safety valve, which should assure him a solid floor for volume. Strange will take a 21-235-1 line on 26 targets through five games into a Week 6 clash with the Texans.

items.headline: Knockout league pickups: Walker, Lamb, McMillan among big names available
items.summary: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.

items.headline: Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns while catching his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Walker's two touchdowns came just 19 seconds apart in the fourth quarter, as he gave Kansas City the lead with a two-yard touchdown run and added a 22-yard touchdown run to create some breathing room after the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. The free-agent addition has paid immediate dividends for his new team, racking up 537 rushing yards and six total touchdowns through four games with the Chiefs. Walker has handled heavy workloads early in the season and will have a chance to rest up during a Week 5 bye before the 4-0 Chiefs host the Chargers in Week 6.

items.headline: Mendoza completed six of eight passes for 48 yards without a touchdown or turnover in Sunday's 45-17 loss to the Patriots. He added three yards on his only carry.
items.summary: With the game out of hand, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak elected to give Mendoza his first NFL snaps on the team's final drive of the game, and the No. 1 overall pick acquitted himself well in a low-pressure situation, with his longest completion going for 16 yards to Tre Tucker. Mendoza even led Las Vegas into the red zone, but he came up just short on a fourth-and-4 from New England's 14-yard line as he scrambled for the sticks. It may be only a matter of time until Mendoza replaces Kirk Cousins under center on a permanent basis, but a switch may not be imminent with the veteran quarterback having led the team to a 3-2 record. Mendoza has at least given his coach some early confidence that he'll be ready when the time comes for him to start.

items.headline: Raiders' Fernando Mendoza makes NFL debut late in loss to Pats
items.summary: No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza made his NFL regular-season debut Sunday with the Raiders trailing the Patriots by 28 points late in the fourth quarter.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Winston, Tucker among top options
items.summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.

items.headline: Tucker caught four of five targets for 41 yards during Sunday's 45-17 loss to the Patriots.
items.summary: Tucker finished second on the team in receptions behind star tight end Brock Bowers (eight) while his 41 receiving yards ranked fourth on the day for Las Vegas. The wide receiver has now posted nearly identical production in three straight contests, finishing with exactly four receptions for a little over 40 yards in each game. Through five games this season, Tucker has caught 19 of 27 targets for 274 yards and a touchdown while operating as the Raiders' top option at wide receiver.

items.headline: Why is Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's snap count decreasing?
items.summary: Coach Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel on why RB Omarion Hampton is being used differently.

items.headline: Hampton turned 14 carries into 33 yards and one target into a six-yard catch during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: Hampton has found room to run in the Chargers' mostly stagnant offense difficult to come by so far this season, averaging 3.7 YPC through five games after going for 4.4 as a rookie in 2025. On Sunday in particular, he had to contend with fellow RBs Kimani Vidal (nine touches) and Keaton Mitchell (six) mixing into the action a decent amount. Due to ceding those reps to his backfield mates, Hampton's weekly ceiling doesn't appear to be as high as it may have seemed heading into the campaign.

items.headline: Nacua brought in 17 of 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown and rushed twice for nine yards in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
items.summary: Nacua's jaw-dropping stat line included new career highs in receptions and targets, as well as a team-high figure in receiving yards. The prolific receiver monopolized Matthew Stafford's attention even more than usual, although the one positive for the Bills defense is it did a solid job keeping Nacua from doing much damage after the catch. The third-year pro also recorded his first receiving touchdown of the season on a picturesque two-yard over-the-shoulder catch early in the fourth quarter, and with his production Monday, he nearly made up for his two-game absence earlier in the campaign. Nacua will take a 31-337-1 line on 45 targets into a Week 6 divisional home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.headline: Matthew Stafford says Nacua 'played like Puka' in return for Rams
items.summary: In Puka Nacua's first game back from a hip injury, Matthew Stafford said he thought the Rams' wide receiver looked like himself on the field.

items.headline: Williams rushed 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown and brought in six of eight targets for 27 yards in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
items.summary: Williams operated as the clear lead back while outpacing Blake Corum by 11 carries, three receptions and four targets, but the former found running room at a premium against a Bills defense that's been surprisingly stout up front. Williams was able to add his fourth rushing touchdown on a dramatic one-yard run with five seconds remaining in regulation to help force overtime, and he's now recorded at least six catches in three consecutive games. Williams should remain in a clear lead role when the Rams host the Cardinals in an NFC West matchup Sunday.

items.headline: Week 4 winners and losers: Tetairoa McMillan, CeeDee Lamb dominate; Jaxon Smith-Njigba struggles
items.summary: CeeDee Lamb and Kyren Williams came up big in Week 4, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D'Andre Swift had disappointing days.

items.headline: Are Ollie Gordon II's fantasy stats sustainable?
items.summary: Are Ollie Gordon II's fantasy stats sustainable?

items.headline: Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 31-24 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
items.summary: Gordon turned in a useful fantasy performance in the lead role once again, even as he navigated a brief exit from the game due to an undisclosed injury in the second half. The second-year back was able to still handle a robust workload despite the Dolphins trailing for the majority of the game, and he finished with a new career high in rush attempts. Gordon also recorded a rushing touchdown for the third straight game when he went in from one yard with just over eight minutes remaining in the first quarter, and he should continue to helm Miami's ground attack in a Week 7 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

items.headline: Washington secured six of eight targets for 43 yards, rushed once for 18 yards, returned two kickoffs for 45 yards and ran back one punt for 28 yards in the Dolphins' 31-24 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
items.summary: Washington led the Dolphins across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets during Caleb Douglas' third straight absence because of an ankle injury, although the middle total was relatively modest on an afternoon in which Malik Willis threw for just 137 yards. Washington's catch total was also a new season high, and he's now upped his reception tally over that of the previous week in four consecutive contests. Washington will remain a relevant asset in deeper PPR formats and as a DFS dart throw in a Week 7 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Stroud, Washington among top options
items.summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.

items.headline: Willis completed 15 of 27 passes for 137 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and added eight carries for 74 yards and another score in the Dolphins' 31-24 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. He also committed two fumbles, losing one and recovering the other.
items.summary: Willis had a particularly difficult first half through the air, and although he was able to bring up his numbers somewhat in the second half, he still finished with his second-fewest passing yards of the season. Willis connected with Kevin Coleman for a three-yard touchdown just past the midway point of the fourth quarter, but the veteran signal-caller made more of an impact on the ground with a season-high rushing yardage total and his second rushing touchdown of the campaign . Willis is helping keep the Dolphins competitive most weeks, so he figures to remain under center for a Week 7 divisional road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

items.headline: How Dolphins QB Malik Willis prepared for second chance
items.summary: Willis has worked for this opportunity in Miami, and he and the Dolphins believe he's ready for it.

items.headline: Addison (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.summary: Addison is sitting out his first game of the campaign due to a sore hamstring that contained him to a pair of limited sessions during Week 5 prep. Meanwhile, fellow WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) is back in action for the first time since the second quarter of a Week 3 victory at Tampa Bay, leaving him as the Vikings' unquestioned No. 1 pass catcher for QB Kyler Murray. Minnesota has a Week 6 bye on tap, so Addison's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Oct. 25 versus the Colts.

items.headline: Vikings list WRs Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison as questionable
items.summary: Vikings receivers Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring) were both listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

items.headline: Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson suffers concussion against Saints
items.summary: The Vikings' injury-ravaged offense absorbed another blow when tight end T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion on the second play of their game against the Saints.

items.headline: The Vikings downgraded Hockenson to out for Sunday's game against the Saints due to a concussion.
items.summary: After recording a seven-yard reception on the Vikings' opening possession, Hockenson immediately headed to the locker room to get checked for a head injury. With Minnesota confirming that he has sustained a concussion, Hockenson will be shut down for the rest of the afternoon and will now be subject to the NFL's five-step protocol. Minnesota is on bye in Week 6, so Hockenson's next chance to play will come against the Colts on Oct. 25.

items.headline: Chism caught five of six targets for 57 yards and added a two-yard rush during Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Chism was able to tie tight end Eli Raridon for the team lead in catches, and he set a new career high with 57 receiving yards. The 24-year-old has now reeled in nine of 13 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown over the Patriots' last four contests.

items.headline: C.J. Gardner-Johnson: Efton Chism III is a 'practice squad player' who 'made a hell of a catch'
items.summary: C.J. Gardner-Johnson dismissed Efton Chism III as a "practice squad player" and said the Patriots WR's one-handed TD catch "probably" will never happen again.

items.headline: Doubs caught one of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Six different Patriots caught at least three passes from Drake Maye as the QB tossed four TDs in total, but Doubs wasn't able to secure a share of the bounty. It was a very disappointing follow-up to his 6-58-2 line from last week given the circumstances, but with his quarterback having apparently regained his swagger, Doubs' own arrow is still pointed up. After getting blanked in his New England debut, Doubs has a 13-219-2 line on 20 targets over the last four games. He'll look to get back in the end zone in a Week 6 tilt against the Jets.

items.headline: Patriots preach patience when it comes to receiver WR Romeo Doubs' modest start
items.summary: After the Patriots signed him to a four-year deal in March, Doubs is searching for his footing in the offense entering Week 4.

items.headline: Patriots place veteran WR Mack Hollins on IR with calf injury
items.summary: The Patriots placed veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins on injured reserve Saturday with a calf injury.

items.headline: The Patriots placed Hollins (calf) on injured reserve Saturday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
items.summary: Hollins was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders due to a calf injury, which is severe enough for the veteran wide receiver to require a stint on IR. As such, Hollins is prohibited from playing for at least the next four games, so the next time he can play is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will all have expanded roles on offense in Hollins' absence, though the Patriots could have A.J. Brown (ankle) back in the fold over the coming weeks.

items.headline: Olave (illness) was limited at Friday's practice and will be listed as questionable for Week 6.
items.summary: An illness cost Olave the first two practices of the week, but he was able to take the field Friday and get some work in. He isn't in the clear for Sunday's matchup with the Giants just yet, but his participation alone Friday suggests it's more likely than not that he'll be available.

items.headline: LeBron James reacts to Jeremiah Smith's record-setting highlight
items.summary: Chris Olave chimed in on social media as well, congratulating Smith for breaking his Ohio State receiving touchdowns record.

items.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Tyson (hamstring) is "progressing well" but isn't on track to return to practice this week, Jeff Nowak of WWL New Orleans reports.
items.summary: Tyson has resided on injured reserve all season after sustaining a right hamstring strain during an Aug. 13 training camp practice. Though the rookie first-round pick hasn't hit any reported snags in his recovery, the Saints aren't yet ready to open his 21-day practice window. Adam Schefter of ESPN previously reported that Tyson wouldn't make his NFL debut until Week 7, but because the young wideout hasn't resumed practicing yet, a return to game action following the Saints' Week 8 bye is probably more realistic at this point.

items.headline: Sources: Saints rookie Jordyn Tyson weeks away from return
items.summary: Saints rookie Jordyn Tyson, who has been on IR after suffering another hamstring injury, is making progress and feeling good but is still considered to be weeks away from returning to action, sources told ESPN.

items.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Wednesday he plans to keep using McCarthy in a change-of-pace role behind starting quarterback Jameis Winston in an effort to take advantage of McCarthy's scrambling ability, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Acquired from the Vikings on Sept. 28, McCarthy has suited up for both of the Giants' ensuing two games but didn't make his team debut until this past Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Commanders. He ended up replacing Winston under center for five snaps, gaining two yards on two carries and having two of the plays wiped out by penalties. Despite the meager returns in his package of plays last week, McCarthy looks like he'll remain a marginal part of the game plan in Week 6 against the Saints. Harbaugh has given no indication that McCarthy will displace Winston as the team's starter anytime soon.

items.headline: Giants sticking with J.J. McCarthy package
items.summary: Jordan Raanan reports the Giants' plan to keep using J.J. McCarthy in a change of pace role to take advantage of his legs.

items.headline: Berrios (foot) underwent successful surgery Friday to repair a Lisfranc injury, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Berrios suffered a foot injury in the Week 5 victory over the Cardinals. He has since been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season and is currently occupying a spot on injured reserve. It's unknown if Berrios will be cleared to suit up for the start of the 2027 campaign, but while he is sidelined this season, Charlie Jones is projected to handle most of the return duties.

items.headline: Giants' Berrios says he'll undergo season-ending foot surgery
items.summary: Giants receiver Braxton Berrios will undergo season-ending surgery on his foot, he announced Tuesday on Instagram.

items.headline: Sadiq (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots after logging a full practice Friday.
items.summary: Sadiq is progressing through the concussion protocol and likely just needs clearance from a neurologist. The Jets listed him as a limited participant Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET in Foxborough.

items.headline: Jets rookie Kenyon Sadiq has been a necessity instead of a 'luxury' draft pick
items.summary: New York used its second (No. 16) of three first-round picks on the tight end out of Oregon.

items.headline: WR Garrett Wilson deems Patriots matchup a 'big-ass game' for Jets
items.summary: New York knows its first divisional game means a lot for the standings.

items.headline: Wilson caught seven of 11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns.
items.summary: Wilson opened the scoring with a 32-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter. That was his third touchdown grab through five games, and Wilson has exceeded 100 receiving yards twice while working as the top receiver for the Jets. No teammate topped 26 receiving yards as wide receivers Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper (ankle), as well as running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) were inactive, while tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) exited in the second half. Up next for Wilson and the 2-3 Jets is a trip to New England to face the Patriots in Week 6.

items.headline: Cooper (ankle) is being activated from injured reserve Saturday and is expected to be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Patriots, Connor Hughes of SNY TV reports.
items.summary: Cooper earned the questionable tag for Week 6 after logging a full practice Friday, and it looks like the rookie first-rounder will be back on the field after spending the last four weeks on injured reserve due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Titans in Week 1. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) sidelined, Cooper could slide into the Jets' WR2 role behind Garrett Wilson for Sunday's contest.

items.headline: Jets rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. to return vs. Patriots; RB Hall, WR Mitchell out
items.summary: Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) will play against the Patriots, but running back Breece Hall and wideout Adonai Mitchell have been ruled out for Sunday's game.

items.headline: The Eagles placed Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve Tuesday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Bigsby will undergo core muscle surgery for an abdominal injury that he picked up during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Giants. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is also considered week-to-week, so with Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley could be the Eagles' starting running back for Week 5 against the Jaguars on Sunday in London.

items.headline: Sources: Eagles RB Bigsby headed to IR, Barkley week-to-week
items.summary: Eagles running back Tank Bigsby sustained a core muscle injury Sunday that requires surgery, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
items.summary: Brown has been sidelined for each of the team's last three contests while nursing an ankle injury, but his limited session Wednesday is a step in the right direction. The wide receiver will have two more chances to log a full practice and officially move past the ankle issue prior to Sunday's matchup with the Panthers.

items.headline: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith among 5 Eagles ruled out vs. Jags
items.summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, new starting center Drew Kendall, safety Marcus Epps and wide receiver Hollywood Brown were all ruled out for Sunday's game in London against the Jaguars.

items.headline: The Steelers removed Metcalf (illness) from the injury report Saturday, and the veteran wide receiver will be available for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Metcalf popped up on Friday's injury report due to an illness and drew the questionable tag, but the eighth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. He saw a season-low four targets in Week 5 against the Colts, but Metcalf and the other Steelers pass catchers would all be in a bump for more passes if Pat Freiermuth -- who was added to Saturday's injury report due to a calf injury -- is unable to play against Tampa Bay.

items.headline: Purdy completed 19 of 29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks. He also rushed five times for six yards and threw a successful two-point conversion.
items.summary: Seattle's talented defense made life tougher for Purdy than it had been up to this point, as he committed his first turnover since Week 1 and took his first three sacks of the season. Purdy nonetheless did enough to keep the 49ers undefeated. He threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans in the first quarter and a seven-yard touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks in the fourth, the latter of which Purdy followed up with a two-point conversion to Evans. The Seahawks responded with a field goal to tie the game at 29-29, but Purdy led the 49ers into position for Eddy Pineiro's go-ahead 44-yard field goal with 1:56 remaining. San Francisco's defense delivered the game-winning stop as Purdy and the 49ers improved to 5-0 heading into a Week 6 MNF home game against the Commanders.

items.headline: Dan Orlovsky: Brock Purdy is the best QB in football right now
items.summary: Dan Orlovsky: Brock Purdy is the best QB in football right now

items.headline: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Price "should be looking at a sooner rather than later return after" the Seahawks' next game in Week 7, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Price was placed on injured reserve after Week 3 due to a lingering chest injury, and while he must miss one more contest to meet the minimum four-game requirement on the list, he appears as if he'll be ready to go when first eligible in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday, Nov. 2. In the meantime, the Seahawks are expected to get back fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee), so Price may be relegated to a lessened role once he's healthy enough to play again.

items.headline: Seahawks place RB Jadarian Price (chest) on IR
items.summary: The Seattle Seahawks are placing starting running back Jadarian Price on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.

items.headline: Seahawks rule out LB Thomas, RB Charbonnet for Thursday night game vs. Broncos
items.summary: The Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas and running back Zach Charbonnet for Thursday's game at Denver.

items.headline: Charbonnet (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game at Denver, Corbin K. Smith of EmeraldCitySpectrum.com reports.
items.summary: The Seahawks opened Charbonnet's practice window to return from the reserve/PUP list on Oct. 1, but he's yet to log anything more than a limited practice since then. The team now has until next Thursday, Oct. 22, to activate him, or else he'll be required to miss the rest of the season by rule. Of course, Seattle does expect Charbonnet to play this season, so even if he isn't ready to play in Week 7, the move will be made next week. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will continue to lead the backfield, with George Holani backing him up.

items.headline: Yes, it's OK to drop these underperformers from your fantasy football team
items.summary: You don't have to hold on to Justin Herbert, Kenny Gainwell, Coutland Sutton or other fantasy underperformers.

items.headline: Gainwell rushed four times for 18 yards and brought in three of four targets for 10 yards in the Buccaneers' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday night.
items.summary: Gainwell logged his highest carry total since Week 1 and parlayed it into a new season high in rushing yards. The veteran change-of-pace back also tied his season best in receptions and recorded multiple catches for the fourth straight game, but over his first five contests in Tampa Bay, Gainwell's overall role is markedly less robust than the one he filled during his lone Steelers season in 2025. As such, his fantasy value is undeniably capped heading into a Week 5 home matchup against Pittsburgh on Sunday, Oct. 18.

items.headline: Mike Clay's emphatic case for choosing Javonte Williams over Bucky Irving in Week 6
items.summary: Mike Clay's emphatic case for choosing Javonte Williams over Bucky Irving in Week 6

items.headline: Irving rushed 21 times for 165 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 10 yards and another score in the Buccaneers' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
items.summary: The early portion of Irving's night offered no hint the third-year back would finish with a new career high in rushing yards, as he repeatedly scuffled for running room throughout most of the first half. However, he did put the Buccaneers' first points on the board with a five-yard touchdown catch on the second play of the second quarter, and he subsequently ripped off a nifty 72-yard scamper that saw him change direction several times within the first 10 yards on the first play of the second half. Irving would go on to cap off the next possession with a one-yard touchdown run, and he sealed Tampa Bay's victory with a 22-yard rush on the final drive of the night that set up a pair of Jalon Daniels' kneel downs. Irving's carry total was also a season-high figure, and he's now averaging 5.3 yards per carry heading into a Week 6 home matchup against the Steelers on Sunday, Oct. 18.

items.headline: Tate caught one of five targets for six yards in Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: It was a rough game overall for Cam Ward and the Titans' passing game, with Tate's numbers being emblematic of the unit's struggles, and it's not clear how much the back issue he dealt with in practice this week was limiting him. It was an especially disappointing showing for the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft after his 9-145-0 line on 12 targets the week before, but growing pains are to be expected in Tennessee's low-wattage offense. Tate will take a 23-273-0 line on 37 targets through his first five pro games into a Week 6 tilt against the Colts.

items.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Should you start Brissett, Tate or Burden in Week 5?
items.summary: Whether you are 4-0 or 0-4, setting a smart Week 5 lineup starts with sorting the facts from your feelings.

items.headline: Ward completed 23 of 36 passes for 170 yards and an interception in Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Texans. He added two yards on his lone carry.
items.summary: The second-year QB led the Titans to a 30-yard Joey Slye field goal on their first possession and then had trouble even getting the ball into Texans territory the rest of the game. Ward does have a 63.2 percent completion rate through five games, a step up from his 59.8 percent mark as a rookie, but it comes with just a 3:3 TD:INT and 5.8 YPA as the rest of his numbers have regressed. Per Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com, coach Robert Saleh said after the game that he's given no thought to replacing Ward under center, and the 0-5 Titans wouldn't have a lot to gain by switching to veteran backup Mitchell Trubisky as they muddle through a rebuild. Ward will try to find some confidence in a Week 6 road trip to Indianapolis.

items.headline: Titans' Robert Saleh after loss: Cam Ward is our QB1
items.summary: Robert Saleh said he'll stick with Cam Ward as his starting QB, even after the Tennessee offense had an embarrassing performance in a 26-3 loss to the Texans.

items.headline: Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt out vs. 49ers with groin injury
items.summary: Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt won't play against the 49ers because of a groin injury, coach Dan Quinn said.

items.headline: Croskey-Merritt (groin) has been ruled out for Monday night's game against the 49ers, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
items.summary: Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice all week due to a groin injury, and he's not been officially ruled out for Monday night's game. The statuses of Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) will be known once the Commanders announce their injury designations on Saturday's practice report. Washington is on a bye for Week 7, so Croskey-Merritt will have more time to recover from his injury before the Commanders' Week 8 tilt against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Diggs (hamstring) was on the field for Saturday's practice session, Jonah Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Diggs is on the practice field for a second consecutive day. He was unable to play against the Giants in Week 5 due to a hamstring injury, and his official status for Monday night's game against the 49ers will be more clear once the Commanders announce their injury designations after Saturday's practice.

items.headline: Commanders QB Daniels will play, WR Diggs out against Giants
items.summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will start Sunday in his return from an elbow injury, but wide receiver Stefon Diggs will not play against the Giants due to a hamstring injury.

items.headline: Marcus Mariota out as Commanders turn to rookie Athan Kaliakmanis
items.summary: Marcus Mariota left Sunday's game against the Colts with a knee injury, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback.

items.headline: Kaliakmanis completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts. He added 16 yards on three carries.
items.summary: The 2026 seventh-round pick out of Rutgers began the game as the backup to Marcus Mariota with Jayden Daniels (elbow) still out, but Kaliakmanis quickly got pressed into duty for his first NFL action when Mariota injured his knee on a sack in the first quarter and was unable to return. Kaliakmanis didn't play too badly under the circumstances and took some shots down the field, one of which went for a 47-yard touchdown to Treylon Burks in the third quarter, but his inexperience showed as the deficit grew. Daniels is aiming to return to the lineup in Week 5 at home against the Giants, but Kaliakmanis could find himself back in the No. 2 role depending on the severity of Mariota's injury -- and he might be in line for his first career NFL start if Daniels doesn't get cleared.

items.headline: McLaurin (hamstring) was on the field for Saturday's practice session, Jonah Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: McLaurin was back on the practice field after sitting out of Friday's session for a veteran rest day. His status for Monday's game against the 49ers should be more clear once the Commanders announce their injury designations following Saturday's practice.

items.headline: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin inactive after Friday injury
items.summary: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin will not play against the Colts because of a hamstring injury suffered in practice Friday.

items.headline: Allgeier is poised for a leading role out of the Cardinals backfield Sunday at the Rams with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined in Week 6, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.summary: Despite Love being active for each of the first five contests of the season, Allgeier's snap share ranged from 36 to 64 percent weekly, and he averaged 9.4 touches for 32.6 yards from scrimmage per game while scoring one rushing TD. The overall workload thus will increase with Love out, and Allgeier's primary competition for RB reps will be Bam Knight, who has just three carries in 2026.

items.headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive and is designated as Arizona's emergency third quarterback for Sunday's matchup versus the Lions.
items.summary: Beck remains the third option behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. The rookie third-rounder will only enter the game if both Brissett and Minshew are unable to continue playing.

items.headline: Bowman was signed from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
items.summary: Bowman was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad ahead of Week 1. While the 26-year-old is now on the active roster, he's currently listed as the No. 4 tight end on the depth chart, meaning he isn't expected to see much action.

items.headline: Brissett completed 29 of 47 passes for 292 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding two rushes for 19 yards and a seven-yard reception on his only target in the Cardinals' 45-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Brissett's final stat line was deceptively impressive and largely the byproduct of plenty of production amassed over the final two drives when Arizona was already down by more than three touchdowns. The veteran signal-caller capped off both of those possessions with scoring tosses to tight ends, connecting with Teagan Quitoriano (13 yards) and Trey McBride (nine yards). Brissett had previously recorded a two-yard scoring strike to Quitoriano back in the first quarter as well, and the former finished with a season high in passing yards and touchdown passes. Brissett next faces the tough challenge of the Rams' talented secondary in a Week 6 road matchup next Sunday.

items.headline: Brooks recorded two catches for 16 yards on seven targets in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Lions.
items.summary: After logging single-digit snaps in each of the Cardinals' first four games while drawing one total target, Brooks saw a substantial increase in playing time in Week 5. With the Cardinals opting to make Marvin Harrison inactive for the Week 5 contest, Brooks stepped into a regular role in three-receiver sets, taking the field for 39 of 73 offensive snaps. Arizona traded Harrison to Houston following the contest, which should clear the way for Brooks to continue seeing ample snaps moving forward. However, Brooks isn't expected to rank as a high priority in the passing game, with all of Michael Wilson, Trey McBride and Kendrick Bourne ahead of him in the pecking order for targets.

items.headline: Higgins caught both of his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's loss to the Giants.
items.summary: As usual, most of Arizona's tight-end targets went to Trey McBride, who posted a 7-31-0 line on 12 looks. However, Higgins actually had a better fantasy score in some formats due to his two-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Higgins didn't log any receptions or targets over the first two weeks of the campaign, but he's ticked up his production a bit over the past two weeks with a 5-39-1 receiving line on five targets.

items.headline: Knight will bump up the Cardinals' RB depth chart in Week 6 with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) ruled out, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.summary: Knight still will be situated behind Tyler Allgeier, but the former nonetheless is the No. 2 back for as long as Love is sidelined. For his career, Knight has tallied 173 carries for 614 yards (3.5 YPC) and five touchdowns and hauled in 36 of 46 targets for 268 yards and another TD in 26 games.

items.headline: Minshew is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
items.summary: Minshew is the backup quarterback behind Jacoby Brissett for the Cardinals. Minshew has been consistently active for the team, while Carson Beck (coach's decision) has been inactive as the team's emergency third QB.

items.headline: Quitoriano caught both of his targets for 15 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 45-21 loss to Detroit.
items.summary: Quitoriano entered Sunday having recorded just two receptions since the beginning of the 2023 campaign. The tight end made the most of his two chances in Week 5, reeling in a two-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett in the first quarter before later connecting with the quarterback again for a 13-yard score in the third quarter. Quitoriano's performance figures to be an anomaly, and he carries little fantasy value moving forward.

items.headline: Virgil recorded two receptions for 29 yards on five targets in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Lions.
items.summary: A healthy inactive for the first four games of the season, Virgil ended up suiting up for the first time after the Cardinals opted to hold Marvin Harrison out in Week 5 before trading him to the Texans shortly after Sunday's contest concluded. Virgil served as the Cardinals' No. 4 receiver, logging just 13 of 73 offensive snaps but seeing ample involvement during his limited time on the field. While the rookie fifth-round pick out of Texas Tech should be active for the Cardinals on a regular basis moving forward, he's likely to rank behind Michael Wilson, Trey McBride and Kendrick Bourne in the pecking order for targets.

items.headline: Conner (foot) is close to practicing, but the Cardinals aren't expected to open his 21-day evaluation window this week, John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports 98.7 FM reports.
items.summary: Conner's 2025 season was cut short due to a right foot injury that required surgery, and he was cleared to take part in practices at the start of training camp. However, he didn't end up mixing into team drills at any point in August before being placed on injured reserve. Though the veteran RB has seemingly made progress in his recovery, the Cardinals are unlikely to rush him back into action with Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight already on the 53-man roster. Gambardoro suggests that Conner may be viewed as more of an insurance policy, and it's not out of the question he gets moved ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

items.headline: The Cardinals placed Long (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: Long left Sunday's game against the Giants due to a knee injury, which is severe enough for the sixth-year pro to go on injured reserve. As such, Long will be required to miss at least the next four games, so Week 9 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Nov. 8 is the earliest he is eligible to return. In order to add more depth at tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, the Cardinals signed 2022 fifth-rounder Teagan Quitoriano from the practice squad to the active roster.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Ford to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Ford was cut from the Vikings' practice squad on Sept. 29. The 27-year-old appeared in 57 regular-season games for the Browns since being drafted in 2022, amassing 340 carries for 1,463 yards and seven touchdowns while catching 107 passes for 647 yards and five scores. Ford could be added to the active roster at some point, though that still wouldn't necessarily mean he will get on the field.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Yeboah to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: With Hunter Long (knee) on injured reserve, the Cardinals addressed the tight end position by signing Teagan Quitoriano from the practice squad to the active roster, with Yeboah taking Quitoriano's place on the scout team. Yeboah last saw regular-season action in 2024 with the Jets, when he contributed on both offense and special teams, and finished with five catches (on eight targets) for 47 yards and a touchdown across nine games.

items.headline: Branch caught both of his targets for 10 yards while also adding 65 kickoff-return yards and 25 yards as a punt returner during Monday night's 45-24 win over the Saints.
items.summary: Branch garnered exactly two targets for the third game in a row as he played 13 snaps on offense. The wide receiver is primarily a special-teams asset, making him an unappealing fantasy option. As long as Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus are available, Branch has little to no offensive upside.

items.headline: Dotson caught two of four passes for 54 yards during the Falcons' 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
